items.scene: at the door of a small restaurant or shop
items.note: てもいいですか (te mo ii desu ka) asks permission — literally 'even if I do this, is it OK?' → 'may I ___?'. It attaches to a verb's て-form, here 入って (haitte, from 入る, 'to enter').

items.scene: at a restaurant entrance
items.note: していません (shite imasen) means you haven't done it, so this is literally "I haven't reserved".

items.target: パスポートをお願いします

items.english: Is this your first time in Japan?
items.scene: small talk with a stranger

items.target: ご注文はお決まりですか
items.scene: what a restaurant server asks
items.note: お決まり (okimari) is the polite noun form of 決まる (kimaru, 'to be decided') — literally asks whether your order is decided.

items.target: アレルギーはありますか
items.scene: what a restaurant server asks

items.target: アレルギーはないです
items.note: ない (nai) is the plain negative of あります (arimasu, "there is").

items.english: Are there any foods you don't like?
items.target: 苦手な食べ物はありますか
items.scene: what a restaurant server asks
items.note: 苦手 (nigate) means something you don't get on with, so this asks about dislikes, not allergies.

items.english: Is there anything you can't eat?
items.target: 食べられないものはありますか
items.scene: what a restaurant server asks
items.note: 食べられない (taberarenai) is the potential negative of 食べる (taberu, 'to eat') — broader than allergies or dislikes, covering anything you're unable to eat for any reason. Common before a set menu or a ryokan dinner.
A good answer to both アレルギーはありますか (arerugī wa arimasu ka, 'Do you have any allergies?') and 食べられないものはありますか (taberarenai mono wa arimasu ka, 'Is there anything you can't eat?').

items.english: Would you like something to drink?
items.target: お飲み物はいかがですか
items.scene: what a restaurant server asks

items.english: What would you like to drink?
items.target: お飲み物は何になさいますか
items.scene: what a restaurant server asks
items.note: なさいます (nasaimasu) is the polite form of します (shimasu, "do"), used by staff to customers.

items.target: 店内でお召し上がりですか
items.scene: what a café or fast-food cashier asks
items.note: お召し上がり (omeshiagari) is the polite way staff say "eat". Answer with 店内でお願いします (tennai de onegaishimasu, "to eat here, please") or 持ち帰りでお願いします (mochikaeri de onegaishimasu, "to take away, please").

items.target: いえいえ、まだまだです
items.scene: replying when someone praises your Japanese
items.note: The modest, expected reply. Saying ありがとうございます (arigatō gozaimasu, "thank you") on its own can sound like you agree you are good.

items.english: I only speak a little Japanese.
items.target: 日本語は少しだけです
items.note: だけ (dake, 'only/just') attaches directly after the word it limits — here 少し (sukoshi, 'a little').

items.target: ゆっくりお願いします

items.scene: what staff say when they take your order or request
items.note: A very polite "understood", used by staff to customers.

items.target: 試着してもいいですか
items.scene: in a clothes shop
items.note: Same ~てもいいですか (te mo ii desu ka, 'may I ___?') pattern as 入ってもいいですか (haitte mo ii desu ka, 'may I come in?'), here attached to 試着する (shichaku suru, 'to try on').
An adjective, not a verb, so the thing you want takes が (ga), not を (o): これが欲しいです (kore ga hoshii desu, 'I want this'). Often written in kana, ほしい. For wanting to DO something, use たい (tai).
items.reviewNote: Owner request 2026-11-04: cover wanting a thing (ほしい) and wanting to do (たい), plus asking how to buy or use something.

items.note: Attaches to a verb's ます-stem: 買います (kaimasu, 'buy') becomes 買いたいです (kaitai desu, 'I want to buy'), and 行きます (ikimasu, 'go') becomes 行きたいです (ikitai desu, 'I want to go'). It changes like an い-adjective, so 'don't want to' is たくないです (takunai desu).

items.note: Fine with friends. Asking a stranger outright what they want sounds blunt, so shop staff say 何かお探しですか (nanika osagashi desu ka, 'Are you looking for something?') instead.

items.note: 買いたい (kaitai, 'want to buy') is 買います (kaimasu, 'buy') plus たい (tai). With たい the thing can take を (o) or が (ga); を is more common in speech. With 欲しい (hoshii) it is always が.

items.note: どうやって (dō yatte) asks how to do something, and 買います (kaimasu) is 'buy'. Swap the verb for other questions: どうやって使いますか (dō yatte tsukaimasu ka, 'How do I use it?').

items.scene: asking a passer-by or staff for help at a machine
items.note: んですが (n desu ga) softens what you just said and leads into the question, the usual polite way to ask for help. どうやって買いますか (dō yatte kaimasu ka) is 'how do I buy it?'.

items.note: 使い方 (tsukaikata, 'how to use') is the stem of 使います (tsukaimasu, 'use') plus 方 (kata, 'way'). 機械 (kikai) is 'machine', and わかりません (wakarimasen) is 'I don't understand'.
items.reviewNote: Owner request 2026-11-04: cover wanting a thing (ほしい) and wanting to do (たい), plus asking how to buy or use something.

items.note: 使い方 (tsukaikata) is 'how to use'. 教えて (oshiete) is the て-form of 教えます (oshiemasu, 'teach, tell'), and て-form plus ください (kudasai) is 'please do'.
items.reviewNote: Owner request 2026-11-04: cover wanting a thing (ほしい) and wanting to do (たい), plus asking how to buy or use something.
